summary: Governed repair phase 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2B.1R.1.1R.30R.3.2.1 -- N-16-5 PAWA HPACWriterCapability Non-Bearer / One-Operation Integrity Repair. RESULT: REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING. Phase-entry SHA R0 = 83b7f70b (== finalized .1R.30R.3.2 head V); A = aff46ec3 (finalized .1R.30R.3.1 head). Repairs the decisive product defect .1R.30R.3.2 independently found and twice reproduced (preserved BLOCKED, immutable, not re-opened): require_writer's only binding check was object identity of a plain, readable instance attribute (writer._authority_seal is self._seal); a caller who already legitimately held one issued capability could copy that exact seal reference onto an object.__new__ shell, which then also satisfied the identity check and authorized a second, distinct registry mutation. Root cause: no field stored on the capability object itself can ever close this class of gap, since any such field is, by the same argument, readable and copyable onto a shell. Fix: a process-local, non-serializable, in-memory canonical-issuance-membership table (_ISSUED_CAPABILITY_REGISTRY, keyed by id(capability), verified by object identity via record.capability is writer, strong reference held for the life of each entry so an id can never be reassigned to a different live object) populated only at the sole construction site (HPACStoreAuthority._new_capability); require_writer now additionally requires this registry membership -- a fact that lives off the capability object and so cannot be copied onto a shell no matter which fields it carries -- and binds scope/spend checks to the registry's frozen values, not the capability's own mutable slots (closing a related, narrower field-mutation gap too). Consumption is marked in the registry at the exact transition point record_write already used for the object-local _spent flag. No new capability field/slot; HPACWriterCapability's closed __slots__ (HPAC-PAWA-REQ-091/094) is byte-unchanged. A defense-in-depth fix also makes an unset-slot object.__new__ shell fail with a clean HPACAuthorityError instead of a raw AttributeError. Contract disposition: NO normative change -- HPAC-PAWA-REQ-102/103's security property (canonical, process-local, non-bearer, one-operation authority, recognised by an identity check, 'not a value comparison') is unchanged and, after this repair, is what the code actually delivers (still an identity check, now two: seal identity and registry-object-identity); HPAC-PAWA-001 stays v1.1 byte-unchanged; HPAC-001 v2.1, RHAMP-001 v1.0, HBDC-001 v1.2 byte-unchanged; git diff 83b7f70b HEAD -- docs/contracts is empty. Independently re-reproduced the historical defect against the immutable finalized .1R.30R.3.1 head (a detached git worktree at aff46ec3, not this working tree) before any edit, confirming the adversary is real; the repaired working tree rejects the identical adversary both via require_writer directly and end-to-end through the real production_writer() -> HumanPrincipalRegistryStore path (enroll_principal succeeds, a forged-capability revoke_principal is rejected -- exactly reversing .1R.30R.3.2 section 5.3's live reproduction). Added the missing adversary regression directly to the existing .1R.30R.3.1 product suite (test_55a/b/c/d, 4 new tests, 95 pre-existing tests kept unedited -- 99 passed, 0 failed) plus a fresh dedicated 24-test repair suite (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_3w_1r_2b_1r_1_1r_30r_3_2_1_pawa_writer_capability_integrity_repair.py -- 24 passed, 0 failed) covering canonical issuance, the decisive shell adversary (direct + end-to-end), bare-shell clean fail-closed, direct-constructor rejection, copy/deepcopy/pickle rejection, restart invalidation, one-operation replay at both layers, token/scope transplant rejection, wrong-role rejection, fixture-vs-production separation, concurrent-use (exactly 1 success of 4 racing threads), sole-construction-site / registry-non-export / issuance-id-never-exposed / no-Slice-2 / hpac_verifier-and-contract-byte-identity / runtime-unchanged guards. One existing test (.1R.30R.1 IV suite's test_require_writer_uses_identity_check_on_seal) had its literal-text assertion updated additively (broadened, not weakened) since its old exact-substring match no longer appears verbatim in the getattr-wrapped hardened code; this is the only existing test anywhere in the repository whose assertion text needed to change. Fixed-SHA attribution (A = aff46ec3 vs R = this working tree, full 36-file + new-file HPAC-touching test surface, 1613 passed / 39 failed / 3 skipped with the repair present): 0 R-only unexplained functional regressions -- the 39 failures reproduce byte-identical on A (pre-existing point-in-time contract/diff-since-baseline guards and unrelated historical test_blocking_reproduction_* demonstrations from earlier, unrelated phases), 2 are working-tree-diff hygiene guards that cleared immediately on commit (confirmed), and 1 is the expected, additively-updated literal-text guard above; one additional test (test_concurrent_conflicting_successors_have_one_canonical_winner, an unrelated hpac_lifecycle.py tmp-file race) was independently confirmed to be a pre-existing flake (1 fail / 2 pass across 3 runs of the unmodified repository, unrelated to this repair). .1R.30R.3.2 preserved BLOCKED, immutable, byte-unchanged, not re-verified by this phase. N-16-5 remains NOT CLOSED -- Slice 1 is implemented with this repair but a fresh independent verification is required before its own IV can be considered complete. Recommended successor (ID recommended, NOT reserved): 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2B.1R.1.1R.30R.3.2.1.1. No Slice 2, no RHAMP credential/counter-state, no enrollment, no FIDO2HumanAuthenticator, no hpac_verifier REAL-mechanism change, no _ELIGIBLE_MECHANISM_IDS widening, no protected presentation, no require_real_assurance wiring through Gate 5/9, no N-16-6/N-16-7, no Slice C, no first external effect, no execution enablement -- all unchanged.
